A scientist measured $5$ particular features, $x_{1}, x_{2}, …, x_{5}$, for each specimen among a group of animals in danger of extinction. The collected data was stored in the standardized observation matrix $X$, where each row contains measurements for a particular specimen.
The singular values of $X$ are
$σ_{1} = 7, σ_{2} = 2, σ_{3} = 1, σ_{4} = 0.6, σ_{5} = 0.4$.
The scientist then converted the original observation matrix $X$ into a new matrix $Y$ using the equation $Y = XV_{1}$, where $V_{1}$ is the $5 \cdot 1$ matrix consisting of the first principal component of the data. What percentage of the original variance is preserved in the new transformed matrix $Y$ compared to the initial observation matrix $X$?

> A calculator is required to answer this question.
